title: When and How Much to Water
summary: Water early in the morning at the base of the plant; deep, less frequent watering builds stronger roots than a daily sprinkle.
actions: Water in the early morning; evening watering keeps leaves wet overnight and invites fungus
Water the soil, not the leaves
Push a finger 5 cm into the soil — if it is dry, water
Vegetables need about 25–40 mm per week (roughly 3–4 watering cans per square metre), more in hot windy weather

sections.heading: Timing
sections.body: Early morning is best. Avoid wetting leaves, especially in the evening.

sections.heading: Amount
sections.body: About 25–40 mm per week for vegetables. Check with a finger; water deeply rather than a little every day.

title: Farming in the Dry Season
summary: With mulch, shade and small-plot irrigation, vegetables can be grown through the dry season near a water source.
actions: Choose plots close to a spring, well or river
Grow high-value vegetables (tomato, chili, leafy greens) on small, intensively managed beds
Mulch heavily and shade seedlings for the first weeks
Use drip lines, perforated bottles or clay pots next to plants to deliver water slowly
Harvest rainwater from roofs into drums during the last rains

sections.heading: Where
sections.body: Small plots near a reliable water source give the best return in the dry season.

sections.heading: How
sections.body: Mulch, shade, and slow watering with drip lines or buried pots. Store rainwater from the last rains.

title: Drainage in the Wet Season
summary: Too much water kills roots and spreads disease; raised beds and drains protect crops in heavy rain.
actions: Make raised beds 20–30 cm high for vegetables in the rains
Dig shallow drains along the contour to carry excess water away
Avoid walking on wet beds; compaction blocks drainage
Remove standing water within a day after heavy rain

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: Waterlogged roots cannot breathe and fungal diseases spread fast in standing water.

sections.heading: How
sections.body: Raised beds, contour drains and no walking on wet soil.

title: Water Management for Rice
summary: Rice needs even, shallow water during growth and controlled drying at key stages; level fields make this possible.
actions: Level the field well before transplanting
Keep 2–3 cm of water for the first week after transplanting, then 3–5 cm
Drain for 3–5 days at maximum tillering to strengthen roots and reduce pests
Keep water during flowering — drought now causes empty grains

sections.heading: Depth
sections.body: 2–3 cm after transplanting, 3–5 cm during tillering. Never let the field dry during flowering.

sections.heading: Drying
sections.body: Drain briefly at maximum tillering and fully 1–2 weeks before harvest.
